claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The paper addresses root cause analysis in microservice systems, where complex service invocation paths and dependencies make prompt anomaly localization difficult and can disrupt operations and maintenance.
claims.quote: Due to the complex service invocation paths and dependencies in enterprise-level microservice systems, it is challenging to locate the anomalies promptly during service invocations, thus causing intractable issues for normal system operations and maintenance.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: CHASE is a causal heterogeneous graph-based framework for root cause analysis in microservice systems using multimodal data including traces, logs, and system monitoring metrics.
claims.quote: In this paper, we propose a Causal Heterogeneous grAph baSed framEwork for root cause analysis, namely CHASE, for microservice systems with multimodal data, including traces, logs, and system monitoring metrics.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: CHASE encodes related information into representative embeddings and models it using a multimodal invocation graph.
claims.quote: Specifically, related information is encoded into representative embeddings and further modeled by a multimodal invocation graph.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: CHASE performs anomaly detection on each instance node using attentive heterogeneous message passing from adjacent metric and log nodes.
claims.quote: Following that, anomaly detection is performed on each instance node with attentive heterogeneous message passing from its adjacent metric and log nodes.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: CHASE learns from a constructed hypergraph where hyperedges represent the flow of causality and then performs root cause localization.
claims.quote: Finally, CHASE learns from the constructed hypergraph with hyperedges representing the flow of causality and performs root cause localization.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: CHASE was evaluated on two public microservice datasets with distinct attributes and compared against state-of-the-art methods.
claims.quote: We evaluate the proposed framework on two public microservice datasets with distinct attributes and compare with the state-of-the-art methods.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: CHASE achieved average performance gains up to 36.2% on A@1 and 29.4% on Percentage@1 compared with its best counterpart.
claims.quote: The results show that CHASE achieves the average performance gain up to 36.2%(A@1) and 29.4%(Percentage@1), respectively to its best counterpart.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: CHASE uses machine-learning-style graph processing by encoding multimodal information into embeddings and using attentive heterogeneous message passing on graph nodes for anomaly detection.
claims.quote: Specifically, related information is encoded into representative embeddings and further modeled by a multimodal invocation graph. Following that, anomaly detection is performed on each instance node with attentive heterogeneous message passing from its adjacent metric and log nodes.
